$fileDescription: CASE-format (openevo-graph/schema/case_schema.json) representation of the 2008 Next Generation Sunshine State Standards (NGSSS), Standard SC.912.L.15 'Diversity and Evolution of Living Organisms' -- all 15 core benchmarks plus a representative set of Access Points (Florida's alternate-achievement-standard tier for students with significant cognitive disabilities). Transformed from real, directly-fetched data (not a secondary mirror): the Common Standards Project API (api.commonstandardsproject.com/api/v1/standard_sets/80B94A122D3D4B95884660FF09CC357E_D1000338_grades-09-10-11-12), confirmed live 2026-10-20, document id D1000338, independently licensed CC BY 3.0 US by the data compiler (Desire2Learn Incorporated / Common Standards Project) on top of Florida's own public-domain government-text status. The Common Standards Project's own data model (ASN -- Achievement Standards Network) is a predecessor/cousin schema to CASE, not CASE itself -- this file is OpenEvo's own transformation of that verified real content into case_schema.json's CFDocument/CFItem shape, not a re-export of a native CASE feed. See case/README.md.

CFDocument.title: Next Generation Sunshine State Standards (NGSSS), Science
CFDocument.creator: Florida Department of Education / Florida State Board of Education
CFDocument.description: Florida's K-12 science standards as adopted by the Florida State Board of Education on 2008-02-19, with the 'scientific theory of' qualifier compromise. The governing science-standards document for Florida from 2008 through the pending 2026 readoption (the 2019-2020 B.E.S.T. Standards rewrite covered English Language Arts and Mathematics only, not science -- independently confirmed by this document's own continuous 'Science (2008-)' subject tag in the Common Standards Project dataset, with no later Florida science document superseding it as of this file's $generated date). This file covers Body of Knowledge 'Life Science', Standard SC.912.L.15 'Diversity and Evolution of Living Organisms' in full (all 15 core benchmarks SC.912.L.15.1-15, plus representative Access Points) -- not a complete re-publication of the full ~500-item Grades 9-12 Science standard set, which also covers physical science, earth/space science, and the rest of life science.
subject: Science
CFDocument.notes: adoptionStatus is 'Active' as of this file's $generated date because the 2008 NGSSS remains the legally operative Florida science standard pending the State Board's expected December 2026 vote on a proposed replacement (see florida-lpm's state/florida/local_policy/records/timeline.yaml, FLLP-EVENT-2026-state-board-vote-expected). Update to 'Superseded' and add a replacedBy CFAssociation once that vote happens. Florida State Board of Education-adopted standard text is a public record under Fla. CFItems.fullStatement: Diversity and Evolution of Living Organisms
CFItems.note: Common Standards Project asnIdentifier S1130831. This is the standard's full, exact title/statement per the Common Standards Project API -- no longer text (e.g. 'the fundamental concept underlying all of biology... supported by multiple forms of scientific evidence') exists at this structural level. That longer phrasing, used in earlier secondary characterizations this repo's founding research relied on, should be treated as a paraphrase/characterization of the standard's intent found elsewhere (possibly FLDOE framework preamble text, not yet located), not a verbatim quotation of SC.912.L.15 itself -- corrected here 2026-10-20 after directly fetching the real data. See state/florida/local_policy/records/mandates.yaml's FLLP-MANDATE-ngsss-2008-sc912l15-standard contributor_notes for the same correction.

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how the scientific theory of evolution is supported by the fossil record, comparative anatomy, comparative embryology, biogeography, molecular biology, and observed evolutionary change.

openEvoLinks.generatedBy: florida-lpm founding research session, 2026-10-20 (informal alignment, not a validated cross-repo link -- see state/florida/lp/records/crosswalk.yaml)

CFItems.fullStatement: Discuss the use of molecular clocks to estimate how long ago various groups of organisms diverged evolutionarily from one another.
Describe how biological diversity is increased by the origin of new species and how it is decreased by the natural process of extinction.
Describe how and why organisms are hierarchically classified and based on evolutionary relationships.
Explain the reasons for changes in how organisms are classified.
Discuss distinguishing characteristics of the domains and kingdoms of living organisms.
Discuss distinguishing characteristics of vertebrate and representative invertebrate phyla, and chordate classes using typical examples.
Describe the scientific explanations of the origin of life on Earth.
Explain the role of reproductive isolation in the process of speciation.
Identify basic trends in hominid evolution from early ancestors six million years ago to modern humans, including brain size, jaw size, language, and manufacture of tools.
CFItems.note: Directly relevant to Pat Beall's Sun Sentinel characterization (cited via NCSE) that the 2026 draft is 'all but erasing' evolution specifically regarding human origins -- this and SC.912.L.15.11 are the two 2008 benchmarks most squarely about human evolution specifically, as opposed to evolution generally.

CFItems.fullStatement: Discuss specific fossil hominids and what they show about human evolution.
CFItems.note: See SC.912.L.15.10's note -- the human-origins-specific benchmark most directly at stake in the 2026 draft's reported omissions.

CFItems.fullStatement: List the conditions for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in a population and why these conditions are not likely to appear in nature. Use the Hardy-Weinberg equation to predict genotypes in a population from observed phenotypes.
Describe the conditions required for natural selection, including: overproduction of offspring, inherited variation, and the struggle to survive, which result in differential reproductive success.

CFItems.fullStatement: Discuss mechanisms of evolutionary change other than natural selection such as genetic drift and gene flow.
CFItems.note: Directly names 'gene flow' and 'genetic drift' -- the exact two terms this repo's research found named as missing vocabulary in the 2026 draft (see FLLP-FINDING-2026-draft-omits-evolution-and-climate-explicit-naming).

CFItems.fullStatement: Describe how mutation and genetic recombination increase genetic variation.
Identify that prehistoric plants and animals changed over time (evolved) or became extinct.
CFItems.note: Florida 'Access Point' (statementLabel in the source data) -- an alternate-achievement-standard tier for students with significant cognitive disabilities, mapped here to CASE's 'Indicator' CFItemType as the closest fit; CASE has no native 'Access Point' type.

CFItems.fullStatement: Recognize ways that the appearance of humans, their language, and their tools have changed over time.

CFAssociations.note: Standard SC.912.L.15 is one of five standards (L.14-L.18) under the Life Science Body of Knowledge.
